ptax.title: Nominal exchange rate
ptax.source: Banco Central do Brasil (SGS), series 1: US dollar selling rate (PTAX)
ptax.convention: Quoted as BRL per 1 USD. A rise means the real DEPRECIATES against the dollar.

reer.title: Real effective exchange rate
reer.source: Banco Central do Brasil (SGS), series 11752: real effective exchange rate index (IPCA-deflated, broad trade-weighted basket)
reer.convention: A rise means the real DEPRECIATES in real terms (Brazil becomes cheaper relative to trading partners). Verified each run from the correlation of monthly changes with PTAX (BRL/USD): 0.65.
reer.transformation: Rebased from BCB's original base (June 1994 = 100) to 2010 average = 100. Rebasing changes the level only, not percentage changes.

ipca.title: Inflation vs. target
ipca.source: IBGE, SIDRA table 1737, variable 2265: IPCA accumulated over 12 months
ipca.convention: Target band: 3.0% centre, tolerance ±1.5 pp (continuous target since Jan 2025, CMN Resolution 5,141/2024). Before 2025 the target was set per calendar year; the band drawn for earlier years shows the target in force that year.

focus.title: Inflation expectations
focus.source: BCB Focus market survey (Olinda API): median of expected IPCA for the next 12 months, smoothed series
focus.transformation: BCB publishes daily; the dashboard keeps the last reading of each week.

selic.title: Policy rate (Selic target)
selic.source: Banco Central do Brasil (SGS), series 432: Selic target set by Copom

real_rate.title: Ex-ante real policy rate
real_rate.source: Derived from BCB series 432 (Selic target) and BCB Focus 12-month IPCA expectations
real_rate.convention: Positive = policy rate above expected inflation (restrictive territory rises with it).
real_rate.transformation: Exact Fisher relation: (1 + Selic) / (1 + expected 12m IPCA) - 1, using end-of-month values.

carry.title: Carry: Selic minus Fed funds
carry.source: Banco Central do Brasil (SGS), series 432; Federal Reserve Board via FRED: federal funds target range (DFEDTARU, DFEDTARL)
carry.convention: Positive = BRL short-term rates above USD rates (the return to borrowing USD to hold BRL, before exchange-rate moves).
carry.transformation: Selic target minus the midpoint of the Fed funds target range. The US rate is carried forward to Brazilian business days.

vol.title: BRL realized volatility
vol.convention: Higher = larger day-to-day swings in BRL/USD.
vol.transformation: Standard deviation of daily log changes in PTAX over a rolling 21-business-day (about 1 month) window, times the square root of 252, in percent.

ibcbr.title: Economic activity (IBC-Br)
ibcbr.units: % change vs. same month a year earlier
ibcbr.source: Banco Central do Brasil (SGS), series 24363: IBC-Br, not seasonally adjusted
ibcbr.convention: Monthly proxy for GDP published by BCB.
ibcbr.transformation: Year-over-year % change of the index. The non-seasonally-adjusted index is used because y/y comparisons already remove seasonality.

unemp.title: Unemployment rate
unemp.source: IBGE, SIDRA table 6381, variable 4099: PNAD Contínua unemployment rate
unemp.convention: Each point is the 3-month moving quarter ending in that month (IBGE definition). Not seasonally adjusted.

ca.title: Current account and FDI
ca.source: Banco Central do Brasil (SGS): series 23079 (current account, 12m, % GDP), 22885 (direct investment liabilities, monthly, USD mn), 24419 (current account, 12m, USD mn)
ca.convention: Current account: negative = deficit. FDI: inflows of direct investment into Brazil (net incurrence of liabilities).
ca.transformation: FDI % GDP = 12-month sum of series 22885 divided by 12-month GDP in USD, where GDP is implied by BCB's own ratio (series 24419 / series 23079 x 100), so both lines share BCB's denominator.

fiscal.title: Fiscal: gross debt and primary balance
fiscal.source: Banco Central do Brasil (SGS): series 13762 (general government gross debt, % GDP, 2008 methodology) and 5793 (consolidated public sector primary result, 12m, % GDP)
fiscal.convention: Primary balance: positive = surplus. Shown as two stacked panels with their own scales (no dual axis).
fiscal.transformation: BCB publishes the primary result as a borrowing requirement (positive = deficit); its sign is flipped so a surplus is positive.
